title: Unified JSON Param Declaration with Typed Hints and Actionable Error Guidance
creator: Asha Nair
description: Problem statement: Engineers integrating tool/function calling face inconsistent JSON parameter manifests across models and SDKs. Current schemas are verbose, lack machine-readable hints for recovery, and produce cryptic runtime errors that are hard for customers to act on. This ticket defines a compact, extensible declaration format for function parameters that combines strict type hints with optional human guidance for validation failures. The goal is to reduce integration time, improve error clarity, and enable SDKs/Console to surface automated remediation suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by API and DX leads describing the declaration format and failure semantics
Runtime accepts the new manifest format and performs deterministic validation with clear error codes
SDKs (js/py) map runtime errors to user-facing messages and suggested fixes for at least 5 common failure classes
Telemetry exposes validation failure types and frequencies to Console dashboards
Backward compatibility: legacy function manifests continue to work, with a deprecation warning emitted when applicable
design_decisions: Use a thin manifest that separates 'shape' (types and requiredness) from 'hints' (human_text and example payloads). This keeps runtime validation efficient and lets UIs consume hint fields without changing core semantics.
Represent primitive types as compact tokens (s, i, f, b, arr, obj) to keep manifests small for high-volume endpoints and prefetched manifests.
Introduce structured 'remediation' hints in plain string form (not executable), e.g., 'try using ISO-8601 timestamp' so SDKs can show actionable tooltips.
Adopt a deterministic error code namespace: VALIDATION.<FIELD>.<REASON> (e.g., VALIDATION.due_date.type_mismatch). Codes must be stable across minor runtime releases for reliable telemetry.

Validation must be staged: (1) fast shape checks (type, required), (2) semantic checks (range, regex), (3) soft-affinity checks (preferential but not blocking). Only hard failures produce non-2xx responses; soft-affinity failures are returned with a structured 'warnings' array.
implementation_steps: 1) Design: finalize compact manifest schema and error-code registry (this ticket)
2) Runtime: implement manifest parser and two-stage validator; add fallback to legacy manifests
3) SDKs: add translation layer mapping error codes to localized messages and suggested fixes
4) Console: display validation failure analytics and per-route common fixes UI
5) QA: craft a 50-case validation test suite, including fuzzing, edge cases, and backward compatibility checks
6) Rollout: canary on internal customers, then staged public rollout with telemetry monitoring
risks: Users may author manifests relying on unstandardized 'hints' leading to UX inconsistencies across SDKs
Size optimization (compact tokens) could reduce readability for humans editing manifests directly; mitigate with devtools that pretty-print manifests
Overzealous semantic checks could break existing customer integrations; mitigate by defaulting new checks to 'warning' mode and promoting to 'error' in a planned release
Ambiguity in error codes could lead to incorrect remediation suggestions; require cross-team review for registry changes
